conflicts.description: D2 [A09] models baseline burn ~24k USD/month (10.4 months runway) and adds a support specialist by M5 plus a Riyadh seller by M6 (40-57k USD), cutting runway to ~8 months. D3 [A12] models a higher bottom-up burn of 24.5-27.5k (avg ~26k, 8.3 months zero-revenue runway) and says headcount must stay at 3 plus a part-time contractor until MRR covers hires. Both cannot hold: the hires D2/D6 need for the 150-clinic Base plan are not in D3's burn, and D3's runway already ends ~Jul 2027. Fundraise timing also diverges: D4 [A20] says start M3-4, D3 [A12/A15] says start M6, close M9.

[A24]/D5 design one in-country cell per country (UAE + KSA), with infra at 400-800 USD/month at 300 clinics, which is consistent with cloud-only CapEx. But [A11] assumes a single UAE entity serving KSA cross-border with no second region in the base case, and excludes the 15-30k USD KSA entity/in-Kingdom hosting cost. The infra opex is small. The CapEx base case omits a residency-driven KSA cell and entity, which D4 [A18] and D5 [A22] treat as probably mandatory.

conflicts.check: Tech stack vendor choices vs OpEx burn
conflicts.description: [A12] puts messaging COGS at ~24 USD/clinic/month (400 appts x 2 msgs x 0.03 USD), ~30-36% of price, and total variable cost at ~28.5 USD. [A25] puts it at 9-18 USD/clinic/month (600 appts x 1 reminder x 0.015-0.03 USD loaded BSP rate). The 2x gap moves contribution from ~50 to ~62-70 USD/clinic and moves break-even by hundreds of clinics. Also [A12]'s burn excludes [A18]'s 25-55k USD year-1 compliance cost and dual-cell infra.

[A29] reports contribution ~62 USD, churn 2.5%, LTV ~2,480 USD, LTV:CAC ~4x, which reads as healthy. [A13] reports contribution ~50 USD, churn 3%, LTV ~1,670 USD, and company operating break-even ~520 clinics at 79 USD flat. That is above the 300 GIVEN target and ~3x the realistic 150 base case. [A16] cites break-even at ~300-340 clinics. Healthy per-unit LTV:CAC and a break-even far beyond reachable volume give opposite go/no-go signals.

[A18] requires in the MVP: consent capture and logs, audit logs, coded optional visit reason with no clinical free text, 24-month retention, in-country hosting, a 72h breach runbook and WhatsApp opt-in for health reminders. [A21]'s MVP scope (calendar, minimal patient record, CSV import, WhatsApp reminders, billing) contains no consent capture, audit logging or breach process (verified: no match in agent_21.md). The 30-36 eng-week scope is already at the limit of the week 10-12 pilot date.

[A06]/[A09] and [A16] set the plan of record at 150 clinics (range 110-180). [A27] sets the base case at 180-230 net clinics with one commissioned rep, a distributor partner, referrals and AEEDC. The difference is whether the added rep and distributor count as base or stretch, and it drives revenue, hiring and fundraise sizing.

There are four different KSA triggers: [A01] after 50-75 paying clinics; [A16]/[A18] at 60 UAE clinics plus a KSA stack plus a DPA; [A26] at 100+ UAE clinics; [A22] KSA cell deployed at M4-5 or on the first KSA contract. At the modelled pace, M4-5 corresponds to ~20-40 clinics, which breaks every clinic-count gate.

Churn ranges from 2% [A06] to 2.5% [A29], 3% [A13] and 3-5% [A17]. These are overlapping ASSUMED ranges, not a contradiction. The blueprint uses 2.5-3% as base and 4%+ as a trip-wire. Each source's figure stays inside its own model.

[A08] has the pilot in Jan 2027 and paid launch in Feb 2027 (~720 h). [A21] has the pilot at week 10-12 (mid/late Jan 2027) with 30-36 eng-weeks. Consistent. This is valid only if the compliance scope addition in the MVP check is absorbed without slipping the date.
